instruction.text: Read the text and answer the question.

atoms.text: Alice wants to test how air resistance affects paper cones of different sizes by dropping them and timing how long it takes for them to reach the ground.

atoms.a: What must Alice keep the same in her experiment to achieve fair results?
b: ++the height the cones are dropped from

feedback.finish: The height from which Alice drops the cones must remain constant to ensure that only the effect of the size of the paper cones on air resistance is being tested.

instruction.text: Alice makes three paper cones of different diameters. Use the following image to fill in Alice’s table.

trainers.layout:
a1 b1
a2 b2
a3 b3
a4 b4

atoms.a: What should Alice use to measure how fast each cone reaches the ground?

feedback.wrong1: It is possible to see which cone is fastest just by looking, but there are more reliable methods to record the speed of the cones.
feedback.wrong2: Rulers, set squares and protractors measure lengths and angles, so they cannot help Alice measure the speed of the cones in her experiment.
feedback.wrong3: Thermometers measure temperature, which is not a factor in Alice’s experiment.

correct.text: A stopwatch is the most useful and reliable tool for Alice’s experiment. It will give specific times that can be used to compare the different cones quantitatively (with numbers).
correct.sound: A stopwatch is the most useful and reliable tool for Alice’s experiment. It will give specific times that can be used to compare the different cones quantitatively, with numbers.

instruction.text: Watch Alice drop the cones from the same height and see what happens.
Use the image to complete Alice’s table of results.

instruction.text: Connect the points on the graph to identify the trend in Alice’s experiment.
Based on the experiment, are the following statements true or false?

atoms.a: The cone’s size does not affect how much air resistance it experiences.
The bigger the surface area of the cone, the more air resistance it experiences and the slower it moves through air.
